evidence: "If it won't step back" picks up the section's own opening question ("What are you afraid would happen if you stepped back?") and the paragraph answers that situation directly: "That part doesn't have to move out", it can keep watch, settle for "blinds tilted open a crack", and "If it says no, I'd listen"; "it" is the guard and "That part" now reads cleanly as the part the heading names. The paragraph's "move out" and "living there" carry on the roommate image from the paragraph above across the new heading, but they are understandable on their own to someone who skipped it, so I do not count that as a split; the repeated "step back" and "small step" are earned, not T26 (judged absent). The linter had no findings, I found no other tell row happening, and with its neighbours the headings read as a natural run of things the guard says or does, not a closed taxonomy.
